name: The AI Risk Taxonomy (AI GOVERNANCE CHAIN™)
author: Mathieu K. Gouanou
credential: Member, Harvard Business Review Advisory Council
license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Attribution required. No commercial use. No derivatives. Commercial licensing: contact@aigovernancechain.com
citation: Mathieu K. Gouanou (2026). The AI Risk Taxonomy. AI GOVERNANCE CHAIN™.
description: Thirty named AI risks organized into six mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive (MECE) categories. Machine-readable edition of the free reference map.
usage: For each risk ask three questions: Could this happen to us? Would we know if it did? Do we have an owner for it? A no, maybe, no answer marks a priority.
paid_depth: Scoring, treatment planning, risk appetite, and monitoring live in the AI Risk Management Kit (paid). The full catalog: https://github.com/aigovernancechain

risks.name: Model error and inaccuracy
risks.definition: The system produces wrong outputs within its intended use.

risks.name: Model drift
risks.definition: Performance degrades silently as the world changes around a static model.

risks.name: Robustness failure
risks.definition: The system breaks on inputs outside its training distribution.

risks.name: Adversarial manipulation
risks.definition: A bad actor crafts inputs to force a harmful output.

risks.name: Hallucination and fabrication
risks.definition: The system invents facts, citations, or confident falsehoods.

categories.name: Data Risks
categories.definition: The inputs are flawed or mishandled.

risks.name: Training data bias
risks.definition: Skewed data teaches the model a skewed view of the world.

risks.name: Data quality failure
risks.definition: Incomplete, stale, or mislabeled data corrupts outputs.

risks.name: Privacy violation
risks.definition: Personal data is used or exposed without basis or consent.

risks.name: Data provenance failure
risks.definition: The origin and rights of training data cannot be established.

risks.name: Data security breach
risks.definition: Training data or prompts are exfiltrated.

categories.name: Ethical and Societal Risks
categories.definition: The system harms people or the public good.

risks.name: Discrimination and unfair outcomes
risks.definition: The system treats groups inequitably.

risks.name: Sycophancy and truthfulness failure
risks.definition: The system agrees, flatters, or tells people what they want to hear instead of what is true.

risks.name: Manipulation and dark patterns
risks.definition: The system nudges people against their interest.

risks.name: Erosion of human autonomy
risks.definition: People defer to the system and stop deciding.

risks.name: Societal and labor disruption
risks.definition: Automation displaces work faster than institutions adapt.

risks.name: Regulatory non-compliance
risks.definition: The system violates the EU AI Act, sector rules, or local law.

risks.name: Liability exposure
risks.definition: Harm caused by the system creates legal claims.

risks.name: Intellectual property infringement
risks.definition: Training or outputs breach copyright or licensing.

risks.name: Contractual and disclosure failure
risks.definition: The organization misrepresents what its AI does.

risks.name: Cross-border conflict
risks.definition: The system meets contradictory rules across jurisdictions.

categories.name: Operational Risks
categories.definition: The organization cannot run or control the system.

risks.name: Lack of human oversight
risks.definition: No one can meaningfully intervene.

risks.name: No off switch
risks.definition: The system cannot be stopped quickly and safely.

risks.name: Vendor and supply-chain dependency
risks.definition: A third-party model or service fails or changes.

risks.name: Monitoring blind spots
risks.definition: Failures occur with no detection.

risks.name: Skills and capacity gap
risks.definition: The people running the system cannot govern it.

categories.name: Strategic and Existential Risks
categories.definition: The system threatens the mission or beyond.

risks.name: Reputational damage
risks.definition: A public failure destroys trust faster than any control can rebuild it.

risks.name: Mission misalignment
risks.definition: The system optimizes for a goal that conflicts with the organization's purpose.

risks.name: Agentic over-reach
risks.definition: An autonomous system takes consequential actions beyond intended scope.

risks.name: Concentration and lock-in
risks.definition: Dependence on a single model or provider becomes irreversible.

risks.name: Frontier and emergent risk
risks.definition: The most advanced systems behave in ways no one anticipated.
